solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heathen trend spread instantly

indicators.note: spread here means scattered about, so the letters of the two words are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A heathen fashion catches on at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' tells you to rearrange the twelve letters of HEATHEN and TREND together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means on the spot, at that very moment, which is what instantly says.

clue.text: There's love in monsieur's proposition

indicators.note: in tells you the word for love is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: the word there taken as written; the 's is only possessive
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, the French title

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's romantic suggestion contains a declaration of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monsieur's' supplies only its initial as the usual French title abbreviation; 'in' places the love symbol among the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical statement put forward to be proved is a proposition, the formal sense.

clue.text: Yours truly in goal? Correct

indicators.note: in signals that the setter's word for themself goes inside the word for goal

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
yours truly is a jokey way for a speaker to say me

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper says he's the one in goal, and asks to be told he's right.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or improve it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Forthcoming bonus docked on account of time

indicators.note: docked means cut short, like a tail, so the last letter of the word for bonus is lost

parts.note: an extra is a bonus, something additional
over can mean concerning or on account of, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: A worker's bonus is cut because of time-keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' removes the final letter of the bonus word, as a tail is docked.
explanation.definitionFit: A forthcoming person is outgoing and sociable, the defining trait of an outgoing personality type.

clue.text: News about motoring organisation that barely gets raised

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the letters for news go round the motoring body

parts.note: N stands for new, so two Ns serve as news
the AA is the Automobile Association, a British breakdown and motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A news story about the AA that hardly lifts anyone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the flatbread is only lightly leavened, so it barely rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian flatbread is made with little leavening, so the dough rises only slightly.

clue.text: Revival of unknown movement with a clear determination

indicators.note: revival is taken as re-vival, a bringing back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: Y is an unknown in algebra
a tic is an involuntary movement
to clear a sum is to net it as profit

explanation.surface: Bringing back an obscure movement with a clear sense of purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, TIC, A and NET run together and are then read backwards as a block.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is dogged persistence, a synonym of determination.

clue.text: Encourage good vitality in European banks

indicators.note: in places the good-and-vitality letters inside the edges of the next word
the banks of a river are its edges, so only the outside letters of European are used

parts.note: go means energy or vitality, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Urging good vigour among Europe's banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to urge someone on, a synonym of encourage.

clue.text: Wretch thrown in heap on the grass

parts.note: a worm is a contemptible, wretched person
cast means thrown, as with a line or dice

explanation.surface: A miserable person is tossed onto a pile on the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil of soil excreted by an earthworm sits as a little pile on a lawn.

clue.text: Extract drug (legal)

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
licit means lawful or legal

explanation.surface: A drug extract is described as legal.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out information or a reaction from someone is to extract it.

clue.text: This makes it hard to contemplate studies before school

definitions.text: This makes it hard to contemplate

indicators.note: before places the word for studies ahead of the word for school

parts.note: to eye something is to study it closely
to train is to school or teach

explanation.surface: Reading up before lessons strains concentration.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired eyes make looking at things difficult, so this condition hinders gazing or contemplating.

clue.text: Some gung-ho ulcerous fiend

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gung-ho villain with ulcers is a nasty brute.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit that robs graves is a kind of fiend or demon.

clue.text: Report looked at leading tabloid

indicators.note: report means a spoken account, so the word for looked at is taken by how it is said

parts.note: read, past tense, means looked at, as in read the paper
top means leading or foremost

explanation.surface: A report says someone read the leading tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense READ is said like RED. A red-top is a British tabloid, from the red masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: British downmarket tabloids are called this after the red banner across their front pages.

clue.text: Internet publication covering working in business

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the online publication goes round the word for working

parts.note: an e-comic is a comic published online
on means working or operating, as with a switch

explanation.surface: An online magazine reports on working in business.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic means relating to trade and commerce, as in an economic or business sense.

clue.text: Overheard order for brawn or shellfish

indicators.note: overheard means heard spoken, so the word for brawn is used for its sound

parts.note: muscle is physical strength or brawn

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a request for brawn or seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brawn' looks like the food (a meat jelly) beside shellfish, but it means strength.
explanation.definitionFit: This bivalve mollusc is a common edible shellfish.

clue.text: Store winnings in container in the kitchen

parts.note: stock is a store or supply
the pot is the pool of winnings in a game

explanation.surface: Keep your prize money in a kitchen jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deep pan for making soup bases is a cooking vessel used in kitchens.

clue.text: Sun's agony aunt regularly involved in tasteless articles still?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun; the 's is possessive

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so the picked letters sit inside the word for tasteless articles

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless goods

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper's agony aunt writes about junk that doesn't sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of the agony aunt phrase. The question mark flags still as describing water, given by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is motionless and still, often stale as well.

clue.text: Thanks from gangster initially discourteous about misbehaving

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of gangster is used
about means going round, so the rude word surrounds the word for misbehaving

parts.note: rude means discourteous
at it means up to mischief, misbehaving

explanation.surface: A gangster is grateful though rudely behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sends the misbehaving phrase inside the rude word, just after its first letter; 'misbehaving' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressing thanks is showing gratitude, a near synonym as a noun.

clue.text: Swear military order barked out in hatred

parts.note: to aver is to declare or swear something is true

indicators.note: barked out means shouted, so the military command is taken by its sound

parts.note: shun is the clipped parade-ground command for attention

explanation.surface: A sergeant swears while barking orders in a fit of loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is strong dislike, close in sense to hatred.

clue.text: Adult pivoted turning parental

parts.note: A is the film classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: turning means the letters of pivoted are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A grown-up spins round, acting like a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoptive describes a parent by adoption, so it is a parental relationship.

clue.text: A milk cart could be viable

parts.note: a float, or milk float, is the small electric van British milkmen deliver in

explanation.surface: A milk delivery vehicle might be a going concern.
explanation.definitionFit: A business afloat is solvent and able to carry on, so it is viable.

clue.text: Ran Germany's trade abroad

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: abroad means all over the place, so the letters of trade are mixed up

explanation.surface: Germany's overseas trade has gone fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move quickly, so darted is a past-tense synonym of ran.

clue.text: Broadcast condensed, not on in fall

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged after the removal

explanation.surface: A condensed broadcast is not shown during autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' says remove O and N from CONDENSED; the remaining CDENSED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall is to drop downwards, so to descend is a verb synonym.

clue.text: The French embracing Britain with detachment that's unenthusiastic

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so the French article goes round the letters for Britain

parts.note: le is a French word for the
UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain
an arm is a branch or detachment of the armed forces

explanation.surface: The French hug Britain with an aloofness that lacks warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means tepid, and figuratively only half-hearted, lacking enthusiasm.

clue.text: Expand Women's Institute's meeting-place

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
a den is a haunt or gathering place

explanation.surface: Enlarge the Women's Institute's meeting hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to make it broader, which expands it.

clue.text: Wish we were there, madam?

parts.note: to miss someone is to wish they were with you
us stands for the we who are wished present

explanation.surface: A postcard-style greeting: wish we were there, madam?
explanation.walkthrough: To miss us is to wish we were there.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is an informal word for a wife, or a form of address to a woman, like madam.

clue.text: Bar is quiet at the back

parts.note: sh is an instruction to be quiet
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: The pub is quiet at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rod or pole is a bar, so a shaft such as a drive shaft fits.

clue.text: Piece of garlic left out for bay

indicators.note: out means left out, so the letter for left is dropped from the garlic piece

parts.note: a clove is a segment of a garlic bulb

explanation.surface: A piece of garlic is left out in favour of a bay leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' poses as the herb beside garlic; it is a small inlet of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cove is a small sheltered inlet of the coast, a type of bay.

clue.text: Look into examination of accounts without computer support being sounded out

indicators.note: into means the word for look goes inside the trimmed word
without means taking out, so the computer letters are removed

parts.note: an audit is an official inspection of accounts
IT, information technology, is the computer support department
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Auditors without IT help complain audibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Read aloud means spoken so it can be heard, which is being sounded out.

clue.text: Introduce a virus and popular old copper's dead

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; the 's is possessive
late means deceased, as in the late king

explanation.surface: A virus arrives as a popular old policeman dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaccinating someone means introducing a weakened pathogen to build immunity.

clue.text: Wayward centres going unheaded stop West Ham for one becoming blasé

indicators.note: stop means plug or fill, so the shuffled letters fill the gap inside the football word

parts.note: West Ham United is an English football club, so United names one

indicators.note: wayward means unruly, so the letters are jumbled
going unheaded means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: West Ham's wandering midfielders become bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going unheaded' drops the first letter, and 'Wayward' jumbles what is left; 'stop' plugs those letters into the club's suffix, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasé describes someone bored and indifferent through familiarity, meaning not interested.
